title: Registry document
description: The one JSON object at registry/registry.json. The gateway accepts or rejects it whole. Source: docs/plan/02-contracts.md -> Registry document, and ADR-0002. Freezes at G1a, except $defs/oauth, which freezes at G1b.

schemaVersion.description: The version of this contract. Only 1 exists. A later shape gets a later number, never a changed meaning.

revision.description: The registry's monotonic version. It must be greater than the live one; a rollback is the old content under a new revision. 'Greater than the live one' compares two documents, so the validator of task 2.1 checks it, not this schema.

apps.description: Every app in the cell. uniqueItems rejects two byte-identical entries. appId, host and oauth.clientId uniqueness is cross-entry, so the validator of task 2.1 checks it. An empty array is a valid document; deployment refuses to start a gateway against one (task 1.7).

appEntry.title: Registry entry
appEntry.description: One app. 'apis' and 'csp' may be absent: an app with no upstream and an app that adds nothing to the baseline content security policy. 'session' is required because the plan fixes no default lifetime.

appId.title: appId
appId.description: 3 to 40 lowercase letters, digits or hyphens. Unique in the registry; uniqueness is the validator's, not this schema's. It names the app's scheme pair, its S3 prefix and its log field.

host.title: host
host.description: The exact authority the browser sends, lowercase, with the port when one is used. Uppercase, a scheme, a path, userinfo or a trailing dot are rejected here. Two rules are not: the host is unique across entries, and it must end with a suffix Policy:AllowedHostSuffixes allows. Both are the validator's. The numeric port range is bounded loosely here (1 to 99999); the validator bounds it to 65535.

release.title: release
release.description: 1 to 64 letters, digits, dots, hyphens or underscores. It names the live S3 prefix, apps/{appId}/releases/{release}/. spactl checks that the prefix exists; the gateway does not.

x-freeze.note: The oauth section is an identity part assigned to G1b. Task I-6 records the G0 report in ADR-0017; the annotated contracts-v1 tag records the freeze.

issuer.title: oauth.issuer
issuer.description: Names an issuer in platform configuration, under Issuers:{name}. That the name exists there is the validator's check, because this schema cannot see platform configuration. Which IIdpProfile applies is set beside the issuer, never in an entry.

clientId.title: oauth.clientId
clientId.description: The OAuth client id, unique across apps. Uniqueness is the validator's. Printable ASCII with no spaces.

clientSecretRef.title: oauth.clientSecretRef
clientSecretRef.description: A Parameter Store parameter and a version, as ssm:{name}:{version} (ADR-0003). Never a secret value: a credential never enters the registry. That the parameter can be read is resolved before a snapshot goes live, not here.

scopes.title: oauth.scopes
scopes.description: The scopes the app requests. 'openid' must be among them.

resource.title: oauth.resource
resource.description: Optional. When present it is one https URL, so the provider binds the access token's aud to the API's identifier. One audience per app in Phase 1.

apis.title: apis
apis.description: The upstreams the app reaches under /api/{name}/. More than one upstream origin on an entry is a warning, not an error: Phase 1 sends one access token to each, which is safe only inside one trust domain. A warning is not expressible here; the validator raises it.

name.description: The {name} segment in /api/{name}/. 1 to 32 lowercase letters, digits or hyphens, unique within the app. Uniqueness within the app is the validator's.

upstream.description: One origin: scheme and authority only, with no path, query, fragment or credentials. It must also match Policy:AllowedUpstreams, which this schema cannot see, so the validator checks it. Phase 2 uses https patterns only.

timeoutSeconds.description: The entry's upstream timeout. Exceeding it is 504 upstream_timeout. The plan states no upper bound.

csp.title: csp
csp.description: Sources added to the baseline content security policy, per directive. Only the directives the baseline sets may be extended; the baseline is in contracts/http-contract.md. A directive listed with no sources adds nothing, so an empty array is rejected.

allOf.$comment: 'unsafe-eval' is rejected in every directive. The letter classes stand in for case-insensitive matching, which content security policy keywords need and ECMA-262 patterns cannot flag.
data: is rejected in script-src. It stays allowed elsewhere; the example entry uses it in img-src.

lifetimeMinutes.description: The session lifetime, between 5 and 720 minutes. There is no sliding expiry.
